title: Discrete geometry and de-Rham cohomology of graphs
summary: We develop a theory of discrete spaces which are built by gluing coordinate patches together into an atlas, much as a manifold is built from charts. Graphs are the main examples, and an atlas on a graph gives it a geometric structure analogous to that of a manifold. This structure leads to a cohomology theory, which we show to be a discrete analogue of de Rham cohomology. We define a "discrete coordinatized space" as a cubical set equipped with the Alexandrov topology, on which differential forms become sheaves.
